key: What was there to be blamed in thee, O Visnu, when thou declaredst, I am Sipivista? Hide not this form from us, nor keep it secret, since thou didst wear another shape in battle.
s: Near the close of a hymn on Visnu’s three strides, the singer turns to one of the god’s names; Sāyaṇa, on 7.100.6, takes it as Vasistha’s plea to Visnu, who had helped him in battle in an assumed form, to appear in his own.

evidence.words: पुरा खलु विष्णुः स्वं रूपं परित्यज्य कृत्रिमं रूपान्तरं धारयन् संग्रामे वसिष्ठस्य साहाय्यं चकार । तं जाननृषिरनया प्रत्याचष्टे। … अतो बहुतेजस्कं यद्वैष्णवं रूपं तदस्माकं प्रदर्शयेति तात्पर्यार्थः
evidence.gloss: Once, indeed, Viṣṇu, setting aside his own form and bearing another, artificial one, gave help to Vasiṣṭha in battle; the seer, knowing him, answers him with this verse … So the purport is: show us that form of yours as Viṣṇu, full of radiance.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, 7.100.6 at [615,6]); the packet’s Sanskrit for 7.100.6 (kim it te viṣṇo paricakṣyaṃ bhūt ... yad anyarūpaḥ samithe babhūtha) is the app’s verse. Sāyaṇa opens with the story that Viṣṇu, abandoning his own form and bearing an artificial one, helped Vasiṣṭha in battle, and that the seer, knowing him, addresses him with this verse; after quoting Nirukta 5.7 to 8 and giving both the disparaging and the praising sense of śipiviṣṭa, both senses end in ‘do not hide this form, reveal it’ (apagūḍhaṃ mā kuru ... tad eva rūpaṃ prakaṭaya) and the purport ‘show us that radiant Vaiṣṇava form’. The reading as given is his and does not take sides between the two senses. Wilson’s note agrees (Vishnu aided Vasishtha in battle under an assumed form). Plain sense faithful: 7.100 tells of the three strides (v3, v4), v5 lauds the name Śipiviṣṭa, v6 is the penultimate verse and the last (v7) is the refrain; no four-word run from the key. Revision 214349 dated 2019-09-26 by the wiki API. Entry-check ok.
